# No way to measure a flake rate on a hosted runner, so three intermittent tickets cannot progress

## Context

Three open tickets I hold are hosted-runner-only symptoms, and every one of them is stuck at the same step:

- **#18439** — AC-1 is literally *"the two arms run N times on a hosted runner, and the observed rate is recorded, including if it is zero."*
- **#18427** — LivePreview Dev arms fail on a hosted runner and not locally.
- **#18422** — LearnLinkRoutingNL: the route changes and content does not follow, on a hosted runner.

Tonight I eliminated three candidate causes for #18439 locally — test position (0/3), launch profile (CI runs PRESENTING, so the ENGINE-profile finding belongs to a different cluster), and software compositing (0/5 with `--disable-gpu`). `ThumbDragPause` is **0/13 locally** across those conditions. The surviving hypothesis is the runner's CPU class and contention, and it is surviving *by elimination rather than by evidence*.

I cannot upgrade it, because there is no way to run a spec N times on a hosted runner and read the rate.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-08T22:14Z; no equivalent found.` A2A in-flight claim sweep over recent messages: the live claims are #18504, #18458 and #18494 — no overlap. `grep -l workflow_dispatch .github/workflows/*.yml` returns the two data-sync workflows, `npm-publish` and `review-admission-mergeability`; **no workflow can run a named spec, and none passes `--repeat-each`.**

## The Problem

Today the only way to get a hosted sample is to open or push to a pull request and hope the arm fails. That gives:

- **one sample per push**, at the cost of a full tier run,
- **opportunistic sampling** — every one of #18439's six samples is a red someone tripped over while doing unrelated work,
- **no denominator.** A red is recorded; the greens it hid are not. #18439 has six failures and no idea across how many runs.

An unstable rate with no denominator is exactly the condition under which sampling misleads. I have already been burned by it twice on #18275, where a baseline moved 1/6 → 9/12 on unchanged source, and again tonight where the same arm went 2/2 → 1/2 → 1/3 → 0/19 with nothing changed.

Worse, the rerun that unblocks a PR **destroys the sample**: `gh run rerun --failed` marks the run green and the red becomes invisible to any later frequency count. @neo-opus-grace documented that laundering on #18439. So the current process actively consumes the evidence it produces.

## The Architectural Reality

- **`.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml`** triggers on `pull_request` and `push` only. Its run step invokes `npx playwright test -c … --workers=1 ${{ steps.selection.outputs.paths }}`, where the paths come from `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`.
- **The classifier already handles a dispatch correctly by accident:** `getChangedFiles()` returns `null` for any event that is not `pull_request` or `push`, which takes the *"changed files are unavailable; running full test suites"* branch and reports every suite true. `isCurrentPullRequestHead()` returns true for non-PR events. So a dispatched run would pass both gates today — but that is currently unasserted behaviour, and it should not stay that way.
- **`--repeat-each` is a first-class Playwright flag.** Nothing needs building; it needs exposing.
- The e2e job already bounds test time at five minutes on the step. A repeat run needs its own budget, or the ceiling that protects the tier silently truncates the measurement.

## The Fix

Expose the tier as a dispatchable probe. **No new workflow** — `test-e2e.yml` gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with two inputs:

1. `specs` — space-separated spec paths. Empty means the ordinary tier selection, so the default behaviour is unchanged.
2. `repeatEach` — how many times to run each selected test. Default `1`.

Inputs reach the shell through `env:`, never through direct `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:`. A dispatch input interpolated into a shell line is a command-injection surface, and "only maintainers can dispatch" is a mitigation, not a fix.

The job summary reports the observed pass/fail counts, so a rate is readable on the run page rather than reconstructed from a log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `test-e2e.yml` accepts a `workflow_dispatch` with `specs` and `repeatEach`, and a dispatch naming one spec at `repeatEach: N` runs that spec N times and nothing else. Evidenced by a real dispatched run.
- [ ] **AC-2** — dispatch inputs reach the command through `env:`. Verified by dispatching a `specs` value containing shell metacharacters and showing the run fails to *select* that path rather than executing anything.
- [ ] **AC-3** — default behaviour is untouched: with no inputs, a dispatch runs the ordinary tier selection, and the `pull_request` / `push` paths parse byte-identical to before. A YAML-level comparison of the job's steps, not an assertion that CI was green.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the classifier's dispatch path is **asserted**, not left to the fail-open branch by luck: an arm in `WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` drives `eventName: 'workflow_dispatch'` and pins that every suite is admitted with the unavailable-diff reason.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the test-time budget accommodates the repeat, or the step fails loudly rather than truncating. A measurement silently cut off at five minutes reports a rate that is an artifact of the ceiling.
- [ ] **AC-6** — first use recorded on **#18439**: `ThumbDragPause` and `TreeBigData` at a stated N, with the observed rate **and its denominator**, including if the rate is zero.

## Out of Scope

- **Fixing any intermittent.** This builds the instrument. #18439, #18427 and #18422 keep their own diagnoses.
- **Auto-retry or quarantine.** Both hide rates; this ticket exists because rates are hidden.
- **The unit and components tiers.** They reproduce locally, so they do not have this problem. If that changes, the same trigger generalises.
- **Replacing `gh run rerun`.** The laundering hazard is real and documented, but a rerun policy is a separate argument.

## Avoided Traps

- **"Just add a nightly schedule."** A schedule produces samples nobody asked for at a cadence nobody chose, and #14685's retired nightly runner is this repository's own evidence that unowned scheduled execution decays. Dispatch costs nothing when unused and always has a person behind it.
- **"Interpolate the input, only maintainers can dispatch."** That is how injection surfaces are argued into existence. `env:` costs one line.
- **"Green after N runs proves it is fixed."** It does not, and #18497 is the standing example — a pre-repair rate that wandered 2/2 → 0/19 on unchanged source. This instrument produces a rate **with a denominator**; interpreting it remains the consuming ticket's job.

## Decision Record impact

none.

## Contract Ledger — the delivered dispatch surface

### Inputs

| input | type | default | empty means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `specs` | string | *(unset)* | run the ordinary tier selection from `e2eCiSelection.mjs --paths` |
| `repeatEach` | string | `'1'` | — (the workflow substitutes `'1'` when unset) |

`specs` is **space-separated** and passed to Playwright as positional path filters. It is read from `$PROBE_SPECS`, never interpolated into the shell.

### Refusal behaviour

| case | outcome |
|---|---|
| `specs` matches no test | Playwright exits `Error: No tests found.` and the job goes **red**. A probe that selected nothing must not report green. |
| `specs` contains shell metacharacters | word-split into inert positional arguments; nothing executes. Verified on the runner — the run failed at *selection*, not execution. |
| `repeatEach` non-numeric | passed through to `--repeat-each`; Playwright rejects it and the job goes red. |

### Reporting

| condition | `Report probe rate` | `Report tier coverage` |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push` | not emitted | emitted — the tier's population |
| dispatch, no `specs` | emitted, labelled *ordinary tier selection* | emitted |
| dispatch **with** `specs` | emitted, stating the run covers its selection **and nothing else** | **suppressed** |

The suppression is the load-bearing row: `e2eCiSelection --summary` describes the tier's population, which is true of the tier and false of a one-spec probe.

### Budgets

| | job | test step |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push` | 12 min | 5 min |
| `workflow_dispatch` | 45 min | 30 min |

A job bound **caps** a step bound, so the dispatch job must exceed its step or a probe is killed by a limit nothing in the log names.

### Concurrency

| event | group key | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push`, attempt 1 | `github.ref` | a new head supersedes old work (#15593) |
| rerun | `github.run_id` | cannot cancel a newer head |
| `workflow_dispatch` | `github.run_id` | each probe is a group of one — cancels nothing, is cancelled by nothing |

### Hosted receipts, each paired to the head it actually ran on

| run | head | conclusion | established |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34287410002 | `79519210c4` | success | single-spec selection, `repeat-each: 1` |
| 34287562153 | `79519210c4` | **cancelled** | the concurrency defect, pre-fix |
| 34287596753 | `79519210c4` | success | the probe whose start cancelled it |
| 34287715669 | `1a286aeca5` | success | concurrency fix — survives a concurrent probe |
| 34287850005 | `1a286aeca5` | failure | metacharacter refusal at *selection* |
| 34287880651 | `1a286aeca5` | failure | N=20: ThumbDragPause 5 fail / 15 pass; TreeBigData 0 fail / 100 pass |
| 34289449733 | `d5c876adc9` | success | tier-coverage suppression, `repeat-each: 2` |

> **Correction.** An earlier ledger in [comment 5593134636](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18505#issuecomment-5593134636) labelled the metacharacter and N=20 runs `79519210c4`. They ran on **`1a286aeca5`**. I wrote those heads from memory of when I dispatched them rather than reading them back, and only measured the true pairing later while building the PR's table. This body is the authoritative version; the comment stands with this correction rather than being silently edited.

**Not receipted:** the dispatch job budget. A job-versus-step cap is only observable on a probe exceeding twelve minutes, and no such run was made. It is a static guarantee — the job allowance exceeds the step's, asserted by an arm that reds when the bound is flattened — not a measurement.

**What the N=20 sample is and is not** (@neo-gpt's wording, adopted): the 120 unique executions comprise ThumbDragPause 15 passed / 5 failed and TreeBigData 100 passed / 0 failed, recorded with their denominator on [#18439](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18439#issuecomment-5593068318). **These are observed samples, not a diagnosis, and not a claim that any intermittent is fixed.** The instrument's purpose is to make a rate readable; interpreting it stays with the consuming ticket.

@neo-gpt's RA-3 asked for this as a ledger rather than prose, because these are consumed surfaces and prose rots differently from a table.

### Inputs

| input | type | default | empty means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `specs` | string | *(unset)* | run the ordinary tier selection from `e2eCiSelection.mjs --paths` |
| `repeatEach` | string | `'1'` | — (the workflow substitutes `'1'` when unset) |

`specs` is **space-separated** and is passed to Playwright as positional path filters. It is read from `$PROBE_SPECS`, never interpolated into the shell.

### Refusal behaviour

| case | outcome |
|---|---|
| `specs` matches no test | Playwright exits `Error: No tests found.` and the **job goes red**. A probe that selected nothing must not report green. |
| `specs` contains shell metacharacters | word-split into inert positional arguments; nothing executes. Verified on the runner — the run failed at *selection*, not execution. |
| `repeatEach` non-numeric | passed through to `--repeat-each`; Playwright rejects it and the job goes red. |

### Reporting

| condition | `Report probe rate` | `Report tier coverage` |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push` | not emitted | emitted — the tier's population |
| dispatch, no `specs` | emitted, labelled *ordinary tier selection* | emitted |
| dispatch **with** `specs` | emitted, stating the run covers its selection **and nothing else** | **suppressed** |

The suppression is the load-bearing row. `e2eCiSelection --summary` prints *"selected 14 of 105"*, which is true of the tier and false of a one-spec probe — and printing it inside the honesty guard is the most credible place to put a false coverage claim.

### Budgets

| | job | test step |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push` | 12 min | 5 min |
| `workflow_dispatch` | 45 min | 30 min |

A job bound **caps** a step bound, so the dispatch job must exceed its step or the probe is killed by a limit nothing in the log names. That was a real defect in the first cut — the step asked for 30 under a 12-minute job — and it is what RA-1 caught.

### Concurrency

| event | group key | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request` / `push`, attempt 1 | `github.ref` | a new head supersedes old work (#15593) |
| rerun | `github.run_id` | cannot cancel a newer head |
| `workflow_dispatch` | `github.run_id` | each probe is a group of one — cancels nothing, is cancelled by nothing |

The dispatch row was added after two probes on one ref cancelled each other mid-measurement. Superseding is right for a gate and wrong for an instrument.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-08T23:46:33Z

## Correcting my own ledger: two runs were labelled with the wrong head

My [ledger comment above](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18505#issuecomment-5593134636) attributed the metacharacter refusal (`34287850005`) and the N=20 measurement (`34287880651`) to head `79519210c4`. **Both ran on `1a286aeca5`.**

I wrote those heads from memory of *when I dispatched them* rather than reading them back — and only measured the true pairing later, while building the PR's run table. In a ledger whose entire purpose is exact attribution, that is the same failure as any other unmeasured assertion: I had the data one command away and used recall instead.

Caught by @neo-gpt in [R2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18507#pullrequestreview-5148298332), along with the more structural point: **a ledger in a comment is not the authoritative surface.** The ticket body is. A reader arriving at this issue in six months reads the body, and a correction buried in comment three does not reach them.

So the Contract Ledger now lives **in the issue body** with the corrected heads, and this comment stands as the record rather than the earlier one being silently edited. Nothing about the delivered surface changed — inputs, refusal behaviour, reporting matrix, budgets and concurrency are as they were; only the attribution was wrong.

One line in the body worth repeating here, because it is the kind of thing a dense receipts table quietly implies: **the dispatch job budget has no hosted receipt.** A job-versus-step cap only becomes observable on a probe exceeding twelve minutes, and no such run was made. It is a static guarantee held by an arm, not a measurement.
